title: Klint Kubiak and Joe DeCamillis Presser - 10.9.26
text: out. Naylor's out. Dante Thornton will not be activated. And Ashton's questionable with an ankle and a foot. Take any of your questions. As far as the foot, [snorts] was that something that happened for Ashton in his KC or it was something practice because it popped up I believe on Thursday. >> Yeah. Not going to get into specifics, but uh you know, he's going to do his best to go. >> Is he going to travel with the team to do? >> Yes. >> What is the concern level? You know, it's that time of year. Guys are getting banged up and if he can't go, then we got to get the next man up. >> Do you think it's something that's affected his performance at all the last few weeks? >> I don't I think I think he's I think he's been doing a great job and again, he's he's a leader on our team. He's a guy we're counting on and uh you know, I I couldn't be more happy with Ashton. We got to keep getting him in the entire offense playing better every week. Um but no, I don't think so. >> Mike is to get more time. uh he hasn't really been that involved in the passing game. I guess what does he have to do to get more involved there? >> Yeah, you know, uh just keep showing us the practice. >> What what have you seen from this Patriots team as you're looking throughout the week? >> Very well coached. Uh high effort, take the ball away. Um just a very impressive defense and that's obviously going back two years. Um and uh have a ton of respect for what they do schematically and how hard they play. Is JPJ good to go for the weekend? >> And you expect him to rejoin the starting lineup? >> Uh, we'll see. >> Do you when you're preparing for a team, it's kind of a mystery who's going to be in the secondary for them with four guys missing. I guess how do you kind of prepare when you're not really sure what roles and who's going to be out there? >> Yeah, you just worry about yourself and worry about, you know, our guys getting better and uh, you know, it's it's the NFL. Injuries happen and the next guy steps up. You talked about needing to put guys in better positions in the run game. How do you feel like you've been able to do that this week of practice? >> Yeah, guys have done a great job responding to to coaching like they always have. And you know, we go into this game and whether you know, there's a lot of different ways to win a game. And so at the end of the day, you know, all we care about is is playing hard together in all three phases and uh you know, whether it's the run game, the pass game, special teams, playing great defense, you know, it takes all those things to win. What variable can the elements of playing outside, you know, add on Sunday? >> Obviously, you know, rain, rain, wind. Um, you know, that's that's that's football. That's the way it's supposed to be played, you know, uh, in the elements. >> With Jaylen out and Dante not activated yet, how does that challenge guys like Malik and Cody to step up? >> Yeah. No, they've been they've been challenged all year and that's that's no different this week. >> All right. Thanks, coach. >> Thanks, guys. How's everybody doing? >> Good. >> Good. What's up? >> Uh there was a there was a conversation before the outside kick last week, I guess. What was going on out on the field? It took kind of a long time for you guys to get get set up there. >> Yeah, I don't think it was anything we had getting set up. Um it was more with the officials and just some things that uh you know, they wanted to make sure they had squared away, but um you know, Matt has done that onside kick a few times. would have liked to have gotten a little better execution on that, but it was still, you know, you still had a shot at it. Worthy has to come in and dive in and go get it. But it's just one of those things with the officials. That's all. That's a it's a new play for them, too. >> When you do when you do a kick like that, there's an element of surprise angle to it. Do you think that time that was spent with the officials took away like gave them time to prepare for that? >> I don't know. I think if we execute the kick better, you know, who knows? But, um, that's something you'd have to ask them. I don't know. I don't I don't think it was something that messed us up in any way. >> What went into the decision on a on a fake, you know, punt attempt where you guys dropped dropped a few guys back and Horizon kind of like snuck in the ball. What kind of went to the decision? >> Yeah, that was a total uh misplay on my part. I got way too greedy. Um that was not for that part of the field. Um and really I should have been much smarter than that because the last time we played Tob, you know, he talked about some of the battles. Well, the last time we played him in Kansas City, we ran a fake, got a first down on him, and we also got a turnover. So, I guarantee he was probably irritated just like I was after this game. So, it's just um that's just how it goes. But, he he got a you know, it was a great call on their part and u you know, I'll learn from that situation and and not get greedy. >> What is the goal of dropping those three guys back? >> We've done it about you know, we did it in the first game too against Miami. So, um, we did it from a little better, uh, position, but, um, you're trying to block people downfield. It's something that a lot of people do around the league. Um, you know, I saw on some podcast where guys, I've never seen anything like that. Well, we scored a touchdown against you, dude, so obviously you have. So, um, you know, it's it's just one of those things that uh, schematically that that you try to work on and uh, it was obviously a bad play at that point in the game. Uh, defense bailed us out though. They did a heck of a job. I think we ended up getting a touchdown on that uh, drive. So, you know, kudos to them. >> What did you see happen on Dariq's fumble? >> It's a great punch by that kid. Uh, it was very similar to Dylan's. Um, we got whipped right at the line of scrimmage when they were or excuse me, right at the point of attack when they were coming down field. And, uh, in my opinion, that's more of a team look, not Dariq's look. Yeah, Dariq feels horrible. All of us feel horrible, but um, we have got to quit the one bad play to where we're letting guys get to the returner that quickly. So we we've got to eliminate that and and that's been a focus this week. >> There was a little just before the fumble there's a little bit of maybe like you know maybe dancing a little bit of kind of getting a little maybe cute with the ball. Is that something that you saw there? >> Yeah. No, I didn't see that really getting queue with the ball. I just saw more um more people there than should have been there. Uh we didn't do as good a job blocking on that play as we need to. So you know you say dancing but you know I'm dancing too when there's 12 people in front of me. So, uh, you know, I I just think we did a poor job execution all the way around on that. And that's again, we got to eliminate that one bad play. And I'm going to tell you this week, we better eliminate cuz this is a heck of a group coming in. They just put Schooler up. They just activated him, which uh if he's not the best special best teams player in the league, he's right up there with everybody else. So, he's he's a good one. Really good one. So, um it's going to be a heck of a challenge for us. I know in playing against Frabel all those years um when I was in Jacksonville and he was in Tennessee, he supports it. He emphasizes it both with players and with how much time he spends on it and the fakes and some of the things he does. So, we got a we got our challenge in front of us. We got to do a heck of a job against these guys. >> The first game that you all are playing outside this season, what kind of variables does that throw into your game? >> Well, you know, you look at the weather reports, all those type of things. Um, luckily at this place, you get a lot of wind. Um, which we've had that during training camp and all that stuff. Now, I was 115 when it's like that. But um I do think the win being in the wind is going to help both Matt and um uh AJ and um Alex on that. That's that's really the three that are the most important. And then the returners also would uh when you do have familiarity with a coach or you know special teams coaches, things like that. Is there almost more of a chess game of like I know what he did, I do adjusted this way, he adjusted this way. Like does that happen? >> Yeah, I mean it does. No question. I mean it's it's it's always a chess game every time, you know? I mean our stuff's on tape. So, I mean, I have a lot of tape, so they've looked at a lot of tape. So, um, you know, they they did a great job last week. But, uh, this is another one that's going to be a challenge this week because Jeremy Springer, who's the coordinator there, was my assistant in LA for the first year. So, uh, when I was there. So, you know, they've, uh, they've got some some MMO on me too there. Good. Thanks,

title: Aaron Donald, Puka Nacua & Rams Coordinators On Standout Players in Week 4, Building Momentum & More
text: How do you evaluate the offense for the first four games of the season? >> You know, it's a it's a loaded question. You know, I think it's uh just I probably similar to every offensive coach in the world right now. A little bit of good, some areas you can improve. Um you know, but I think is as much anything. We were talking about this earlier this week as an offense. It's that time of the year where you're establishing your identity both schematically and the mentality that you play with. And I think that what I've seen from our guys is a willingness to figure it out each week despite who's available, despite the opponent and the style that we're playing. I think that those guys have done a great job locking into the practice reps um preparing themselves to uh go out there and have successful outcomes in the game. There's always going to be things that you want to improve on, areas that you feel like you can grow, and there's some obvious areas for us that uh we feel like we can grow and and can obviously help us even with just the results at the end of drives. Um but again, lot lot of room for growth, some some good things that have happened and that's about where you're at for everybody after four games. >> You say there's areas to improve. Which ones stand out to you? >> Yeah, the obvious ones uh you know, the penalties and just not shooting ourselves in the foot. I think there's always going to be some of the natural causes of what happens throughout the course of the snap. Uh there are things that we can do to take care of stuff that we can control. So that's been an area of emphasis uh for us, especially this week. Um you know, and obviously finishing drives in the end zone. That's that was a calling card to us at our best a year ago. And I think for us, you know, we've got to get um we've got to find ways to get, you know, across the goal line one way or another. And can do that a number of different ways. Got a number of different people we can utilize to do that. But ultimately, that's a huge difference when you're um scoring touchdowns instead of settling for field goals. And um it's a big part of, you know, any successful offense >> when you know that you're going up against an offense like the Bills and a quarterback like Josh. I know you're preparing for the defense, but like does, you know, knowing that you might have to go low for blow like you guys did against the Bills a couple years ago kind of add to any of the intentionality around that? You know what, Sean does a good job every week of communicating to the team how we need to go and win the game. And we're obviously aware that there are three phases that, you know, all got to be at our best, but that can look different phase to phase that can look different um from one phase complimenting another. And so you're always aware of how you want to approach the game as a, you know, as a team in general. And it's, you know, it's always unique. You're out there as an offense and, you know, you're process driven on on, you know, attacking and executing against that defense. But, uh, there's, you know, that's one part of the entire game. And so, us being collectively at our best. But, yeah, uh, it's it's something that Sean mentions every week with how do we have to go win the game against this specific opponent in this environment with these circumstances. And it does it looks different every week. Um, you know, certainly this week in comparison to last week, in comparison to next week, it'll always be a little bit of difference. >> First time, uh, Jim Leonard's called plays for an NFL defense. Like, what stands out to you about this Wilson man? Yeah, I was at Illinois when he was calling plays at uh Wisconsin. Uh it was maybe my second year at Illinois as a as a quality control. And so uh got a lot of respect for him, his career, his background, uh type of mentality that that he has in general. And you can see that, you know, all over their defense with with uh their ability to challenge you with different looks, their ability to move guys into different spots and and honestly have an attacking style. They do a great job up front. uh their front makes their squad go and if you don't take care of those guys both in the run game and in the pass game, you can end up in in some tough spots and um as much as you want to, you know, as much as you can, you want to stay on track and and and not let those guys be able to set a rush and be able to uh pin their ears back and so they've done a good job, you know, early on in this season of being able to do that. So, uh we got to be mindful of that. Um but a lot of respect for him as a coordinator and what he's done so far. Seems like Blake Corum Blake [clears throat] Cororum has had a little bit of trouble really getting started or breaking out. What's What have you seen from him? And is that accurate or or would you how would you kind of describe that? >> I would go with in the only reason I say inaccurate. It's it's like so unique anytime that you have two guys that are playing a lot of reps and and it's hard to sit there and say it's like, hey man, we ran the same play and you know this one we got to a look that we were you know looking for and this one was going to be a tough down regardless of who the back was uh that was in there. I think we got so much trust in our guys for being able to execute uh regardless of of which back is in there. And I think that's the confidence that we have is that we don't care who's out there. We feel like if there's a good opportunity to go and make a play that those guys can go and make and so I wouldn't necessarily say that I I would say uh some of that is, you know, it's week four and you just got to keep going. And um you know, I think some of those opportunities will continue to come his way. >> On the flip side of that, is this Kyron's best season? Is he is he the best version of himself right now at this point in his career? >> Yeah. You know what? I would even go outside of the four games that we've played and say that he was to me the most consistent player, and that's not taking anything away from all of our guys and how they approached, but the most consistent player that we had in the building this off season. Um, from OTAAS to training camp, that guy came to work every single day, rep after rep over and over. I don't think he missed a, you know, a rep a day. I don't think he had a day where he was like, "Ah, we're going to give Kairen a little bit of a break here." He has come to work. And so, I think you're seeing positive results from what was going on this entire offseason. So, I've been super fired up for um what he's contributed to our offense and and I think that's part that you love about him as much as anything. He could care less about his stats. He could care less about what's going on. He just loves being a part of this team and loves being able to make an impact and and he's done that in an awesome way for us. player like so so good with so many areas from rushing to receiving the pass throw. What's the process like for you to figure out the best ways to employ them in the right situations to use those different skills? >> Yeah, I the cool part about our offense is that there is a lot of versatility to it and so you feel like with all of our players that we can utilize them in a lot of different ways and the the players that I feel like we're able to utilize the best are the ones that they bring a lot to the table. it's hard to pinpoint exactly what they're going to do on each given snap and Kron certainly fits into that um realm uh as long as as well as a lot of our guys. Uh but I think for as much as anything because of his approach because he takes every single part of his game so seriously and just with great intent you get the best of him in all those realms. And so that's uh it's been awesome to see. Uh, but it does it makes it more easy as a coach on you and and figuring out what he can do because you feel confident in him being able to do it all. >> He said during training camp that he didn't do any for the first time he didn't do any wide receiver drills and focus just on running back drills this off season. How have you seen that growth in him and you that aspect of the game? >> Yeah, you know what his as much as anything I think it can always be hard for a running back to get quality looks of, you know, even if I'm sitting there and practicing receiver drills, it's so different, man. I'm I'm when I'm running around from the back field, um where exactly that location of somebody who's matching me, it can feel a lot different than just, hey, I'm lined up, you know, split out in the slot in a two-point stance. Uh again, I thought he got the reps, whether he's practicing behind the scenes or not, he got the reps in the course of practice. He's gotten just quality reps in the course of even games. You know, you learn and sit there and man, how have people played him? Um where has he been available? There's a cool rep of him catching the checkdown this last game where, you know, the the first time he catches checkdown, he ends up on a third and short. Uh we don't get it on that next play and five plays later, he catches a checkdown, uh gets vertical right away, goes and gets us a first down. And so he's the type that he's learning as the game is going on. He's taking inventory of what's going on and and able to be better uh each rep, each series. So that's what you appreciate about him. However, his approach, you know, is you know, week in and week out. or 11 personnel. More 11 personnel on Sunday just because of the injuries at tight end Kobe's able to play. Do you feel like you can access you have enough depth to access that like the heavier packages? >> Yeah, we feel confident in our depth. Here's what I'd say is I think every week you go in and try to figure out the best plan and the best uh personnels to be able to attack a defense. And that can look different based on who you have available. that can also look different based on what they do and how they challenge you and what you feel can put our players in the best position to be successful. So, what I'm encouraged by, I think the most important part of of what you're learning in the NFL season is um you got to win games in different ways and you know, [snorts] we would love to go out there and say, you know what, we reeled off 40 runs uh got ahead early and you know, just had but the reality is you're going to have to win games in different ways. uh you know in the middle of the season, at the end of the season, certainly down the stretch. And so uh I I like that we've been able to show that that we've been able to have different people out there, different people available, and that you're approaching in a way that you feel like allows you a chance to uh you know, have success and compete at a high level. So again, important part early in the season. Um but yeah, having Kobe and having guys available is a big part of being able to access more personnel groupings. >> Appreciate you guys. How's it going? >> I know just the limited participation, but how did Aaron look back in practice? >> It was good. It was great to have him out there. Great to see him running around playing again. You know, it's been good to have him back kind of in the mix. You know, he got some, you know, kind of his his legs under him in those those couple games he was able to play. So, good to have a good week of prep today and we'll see how it goes. >> You guys got the stop on the goal line on Sunday. What was your reaction? >> Just uh, you know, excited. the guys fought. You know, that was a drive, you know, Sean kind of mentioned it where, you know, they actually did get some runs off in that drive and it was kind of like a little test of character right there where, you know, your first down inside the 10 yardd line. Um, you know, you're down by 10 points that late in the game. That many plays, you know, our guys were worn down and they just fought and, you know, and our theory is, you know, just make them snap it one more time. Make them snap it one more time. That's why offenses always want to score and our guys did just that. >> You guys blitzed a good amount on Sunday and had a lot of success doing it. So, uh, just what kind of went into adding that to what you guys do and after seeing it play out, how much of that success do you guys think it would carry over? >> Yeah, it's always going to be like a week to week thing. You know, whether we blitz or fourman rush or anything, we're always going to do what's best and some of it's based off the flow of the game, some of it's based off the opponent, some of it's based off the matchup, some of it's based off some of our injuries. So, so many things go into it whether, you know, whether you call them or not or have them or not. And, uh, so that's always going to be a week toe thing. Cam Kinchins was a big part of those packages. Like what do you like about him as someone getting out? >> Yeah, he he's a big part of our defense. So, he's always going to have a huge role. Um whether it's those packages or something else. Um he's a playmaker and he's out there. You see that joy he plays with, you see him smiling. He's a ball hawk. He makes plays and uh when he's out there and when he's playing a bunch of snaps for us, a ton of good things happen. So, we're always going to have huge roles for him um in every single game that we play um whether it's, you know, on pass downs or normal downs. and uh he's going to do a lot of the same stuff and we're excited about him. >> I know you view Kobe as a three down defensive lineman, but how have you seen him show up against the run in particular and the way that's affected the unit? >> You say that what >> Kobe Turner against the run like just how he's shown up that way. >> Oh, three down. I think three down defensive lineman. Oh yeah, he's he's all downs. Yeah, he's No, he he's a stud. I mean, it's really been since the day I got here, you know, his rookie year, um I was the inside backer's coach and he was doing the exact same thing and now he's just continued to take it up a level. Um, you know, obviously with Aaron back, it's those two are the leader of the of that room, but, uh, you know, he leads with the way he works, with the way he goes about every single day. He takes no days off, no plays off. Um, and yeah, you're exactly right. He he's really got an all downs and he doesn't have you can pull the tape up of every play this season and you're not going to v a lot of bad plays to Kobe Turner. >> Other guy seems to be taking up a notch is Byron Young. You know, two and a half sacks on Sunday and he's got the highest pressure rate yet of his career. So, I mean, it feels like he gets better every single year, but what did what do you notice that he's added this year that's that's better than what it was? >> Yeah, it feels like the game game slows down for him every single year. You know, I remember remember evaluating him at Tennessee and his four-point stance getting off and then and you know, in his rookie year, he took I think over a thousand snaps, so you saw a huge growth that year. And then ever since then, he's just one of those guys. He's very intentional. Um Joe and him have a really cool relationship, really special bond that they have. Um, and you just see he takes really he takes coaching and he can apply it to the field and you know he's such a special person, such a special player and I and I'm just so happy he's starting to get the credit that he's always deserved. >> How is it different for you when you know you're going to have Aaron going into a game as opposed to, you know, not knowing whether he was going to be available, >> whether we know we have him or not. >> Yeah. for you as a DC? I mean, >> yeah, you're always going to kind of like there's always guys and that's just part of life in the NFL where there's guys that are kind of questionable going into the week. So, certain things like that where you might have a plan or might have a couple things where if he plays, we're going to go to this and obviously you got to be ready if he doesn't play. And uh obviously, you know, you always want to know for certain either way, but you know, it's better to if there's a chance that he's going to play, then you know, we'll take that chance and we'll have some stuff ready for him, right? >> What's the biggest challenge going up against a quarterback like Josh? Oh gosh, it's uh there's a lot of things. Um you know, they they have a great offense in general and they do a great job with the scheme. Um they have answers to a lot of different things and you could see, but you know, he's obviously one of the ultimate competitors in this league. He's a great quarterback just standing there playing in the pocket and then obviously you can see all the off schedule plays that he makes. Um one of the best players, if not the best player in the NFL right now. >> What was the thought process of bringing Eric Kendricks in on practice? Yeah, he, you know, obviously for depth at the linebacker spot and just a guy to come in and help out and I'm I'm just excited to add a veteran presence to that room. Um, I'm excited to, you know, kind of bounce some ideas off him and kind of pick his brain. He was part of some of those great defenses in Minnesota. Um, kind of seeing what they did and starting talking to him and seeing and obviously he was in a similar scheme with the Chargers. So, um, just really excited to have him. He he was really he was he was great yesterday in practice and, uh, just excited to kind of keep talking to him and and grow a relationship with him. Thank you guys. >> How's your back feel? [laughter] >> I feel good. I feel good. Feel I feel feel a lot better than what I was. So that's good. >> What was it that you were kind of dealing with? >> Um I don't know. But just follow the you know um the regimen that Re and Mark had me for. I trust what they you know to get me back right where I need to be. So whatever they had me doing, I did and I feel great right now. Aaron, how impressed were you what you saw uh from from your teammates against >> I was proud. Um I was proud how the defense played. I think they played dominant football and the way the offense kept, you know, kept going and kept going and found their way to win the game with them last two drives, man. I think that was it was great team football. Found a way to win and on the road in Philly that was hard. So, um I think it was a you know hard fought game, earned win. >> What was it like to see just the way that the pass rush guys used? >> I wish I was out there. I was like, damn, I wish I was out there. No, but I was proud of them. I think they played good. They battled. Um, even when I watched it on film, man, even what the guys did up front, um, the way Fist, Kobe, and them guys, they we left some sacks on the field, but um, they affected them a lot, making them uncomfortable and did what they need to do to win. So, >> do you feel Well, you're going to play on Monday, correct? >> I'm planning to play every week. >> Okay. [laughter] Um, do you feel like you are back in football shape and ready to >> I feel I feel good. You know, obviously, you got to continue to play the game. Um, so I feel I feel really good though. Yeah, feel good. >> You know, you think I'm a football shape. [laughter] What you What you trying to say? >> I I just Let me clarify. I meant like it takes a few weeks, you know, for anyone to get to go through training camp to get ready to play. >> I had two holdouts here, so I never had I missed two training camp. [laughter] So, >> but I feel I do feel good. Um, you know, I don't feel like my win's off. I don't feel like I'd be out there exhausted. I think the way we we able to rotate helped me a lot. But um I I do feel good. Just got to keep going. Um try to be more productive, do what I need to do. But you know, that's out there playing the game, right? And but I'm feeling good. >> Were you able to do a full day of practice today? >> Yes. Yes. Felt good. Yesterday I got to practice. The day I got to practice. Um no setbacks. Feel great. And let's keep feeling [laughter] like that. Darren, I asked like Kobe Turner and Byron Young earlier in the week what it does to you when you and Miles don't play to get extra guys snaps that might not ordinarily get snaps and reps and you know how that could longterm give them confidence if they're ever called upon. They they said it could be a really good thing. What do you think, you know, it is for them? >> Well, they they did have a lot of success when me and Miles wasn't here the last couple years. So, um you know, they they've been doing playing with each other for a while, having success without certain people here. Um we just extra pieces to the puzzle. Obviously guys that's here, you want them to be prepared, be ready when their names is called to go out there and perform. And I think we got a bunch of guys that can do that. So, um, it's about trusting the next man up. >> How have you seen Byron grow from his rookie year to now? >> Um, just making plays, man. I think he's just consistent. That's what it's about, being consistent, um, every single year, week in and week out. Um, playing with a lot more confidence, um, and making a lot more plays, you know. Um, hope he continue to do that and make even more plays than what he did last week, this week. So, um, he's playing good football right now, though. when you watch film, how do you sort of break down penalties and things like that? Like what's your process for cleaning it up? As Sean says, >> I don't really look at flags. I just really, you know, break down what I need to break down on my opponents. Um, from, you know, obviously the offensive lineman, different things that I can see, tendencies that I can see to help me play faster, um, try to get myself upper hand. But >> you've played against Josh Allen before, but you weren't here in 2024 when he ran for three touchdowns, passed for three. >> He ran for three touchdowns. >> Did you? So, what what are your impressions of him now? Kind of >> he's a playmaker. Um I think I got to play him. I think my first time playing him was 2020. I think that was his first like breakout year or whatever. I'm like, "Yeah, he's a he's a different type of player." Um I call him like a futuristic Big Ben, more athletic, you know, hard to tackle, a lot faster. Um able to move a lot different. So, um he can hurt you in a lot of different ways. Um he's not easy to take down. Um and he's a playmaker. That's all you can say. So, you got to find ways to keep him in the box. Um, make sure when you get your hands on him, make sure you get him down to the ground, not let him stiff for him. You be able to look downfield and throw a touchdown. So, um, he's a guy that you got to worry about and got to try to find a way of effect. >> how was practice this week for you? >> Uh, it's been good. title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Good. How are you? >> Good. Good. I'm good. Friday. Had a good week. We get to play another game. >> Excellent. >> So, uh, Caleb Douglas, Rob Deal, Reese Taylor, Jackson Woodard, are they all out? Uh, Sunday is the guys who didn't practice last two days. >> Let's go one at a time. >> Caleb's going to run today, so I would say he's unlikely, but he's progressing. Um, Beal will be out and Woodard will practice today. So, we'll we'll see how it goes, but he'll practice today. >> And Justin Jolly, I guess, was in protocol. Is he out Sunday? >> Yeah, he'll be out. >> Okay. >> And any decision on Kenneth Grant for Sunday at this point? How's that? >> Um, let's see how he does today in practice. You know, I want to make sure he can get through all three practices and and then we'll make that decision after practice today. He's had a good week, but I'd like to see I'd like to see him get through it. How >> about Reese Taylor and Jaylen Wright? >> Reese, like I said, he's out. >> Yeah, no, no problem. He he'll be out um for a few weeks. And who was the other one? >> Jaylen Wright up here with a foot. He was limited. >> Yeah, he should be he should be good to go. >> Are you at the point with Storm Doug where he's ready to play and you just have to make decision on one of these weeks? Uh or does he still need more time, you think? Um, I think it's a combination of both, you know, so we'll we'll keep seeing how he's doing. >> If Jamar Chase plays when Chris Johnson lines up against them, what do you want to see? >> Um, I want to see him rely on his fundamentals and techniques. I want him to see him continue to improve. I think, you know, that that's a that's a fair question. You're talking about a rookie. I'm sure that's why you're asking against, you know, maybe the premier receiver in all of our league. Um, I have a ton of respect for Jamar after watching him live last year for the first time, really getting to coach against him. Um, I love the way he plays and like I said, I think he's the guy. Um, what happens a lot of the time is when you start to think about that as a player and you start to, you know, go away from your fundamentals and techniques and you try to change who you are, you play, you don't play very well. So, you know, you got to know who you're up against, right? I'd be crazy to tell you that you can't do that. But you you've got to rely on your training. I mean, you got to play with great eyes, great feet, great physicality. You got to finish violent at the reception point. You got to understand where your help is and play with the leverage to your help. Um, and you got to be physical and you got to be aggressive because you're going to have to match that because that's how he plays the game. I want him to I want to see him be himself and I want to see him take a step. And that would be my my answer to your question if that makes sense. coach, what what's the significance of getting that first win within the process knowing that it's still early? >> Yeah. Um, you know, I just probably more for the players, you know, all the hard work they've put in. Um, you know, h how much I think they've improved and, you know, I I I think for them for us to win would be a great reward for the players. I mean, that's that that's important and that that what I say is the biggest thing for me is is for the players. >> When it comes to the run game, are you somebody that likes to ride the high end or are you committed to the committee approach? >> Um, both. And I know that's not what you want to hear. If if you get into a drive and a guy is hot, I think you got to keep going. Um, but then all of a sudden, if that guy gets really tired and he thinks he still wants to keep going, but he can't, you got to make a good decision and and get somebody else in. Um, but I just just like with any player at any position, you can get into a a really good routine, right? And and when a guy gets into a good routine and he starts to feel really comfortable and he's playing well, you want to watch that and you want that guy to keep going. Um, but you can't go forever at that position. So, you know, there's there's hopefully a lot of plays and you're going to have to use multiple players. Um, it's like, you know, some people like to rotate corners in and out and I've done it in my career, but some guys got to get in a rhythm and they got to get they got to get playing and their feet in the ground and a feel for the game and the more the game goes on, the better some of them get. And running back is the same thing. So, both >> one of the Bengals defensive backs told reporters yesterday that they think they have a tell on Malik Willis that they'll go they plan to break on the ball when he taps it. >> Is that something that needs to be addressed? Is it a concern? Um, I played high school quarterback. I had I did the same thing. It never hurt me. I'm just joking. Um, but I did play high school quarterback and I probably patted the ball. Being very honest with you, I've studied quarterbacks for over 25 years and that is not uncommon. A lot of quarterbacks pat the ball or take their hand off the ball. I mean, there's some I've studied that look up right before they throw the ball. I I just I don't think there's anything revolutionary about that. It's a timing and rhythm thing with a lot of guys and there's a lot of them that do that. Um but any opponent that wants to share our tendencies with us, we'll we'll take any time. So, uh but there's there's nothing there on that. And I if there was something big like he told us every time our left guard was in a three-point stance, we were running the ball, I'd be like, "All right, we got to fix that." It's just there's nothing there. >> Have uh the absence of Caleb Douglas and Devon Han. >> Yeah. >> How has that impacted the team most? I mean, does it fall on Sloic? Does it fall on offensive line, Malik Willis, the defense? How what's been the effect? >> I mean, look, you lose you lose two guys who are playing really well and you lose, you know, one of the best running backs in the NFL. But that's our sport. I mean, so it's it's got to be it's why I talk about developing our players. It's why you asked me the other day, why are we doing those seven on sevens? Why are we doing Sunday practices? You have to have your other guys ready to go. Um, and certainly is it a heartbreaker when it's like one of the best players in the league? Yeah. But our team's got to go forward. That that unfortunately that's part of our game, right? So, we we've got to recognize it. We've got to coach, we've got to develop. Our players need to step up. Our coaches need to step up. And we all got to do it together. Um, but that's football. >> Coach, >> you kind of offered, for lack of a better words, a a challenge to Chop earlier this week, saying, you know, that's that's great. Let's see you do it again. Let's see you put in another good week of practice. How have you seen him respond as he's looking to string now three good games in a row together? >> Just just like I thought he would. I mean, he's had a great week of practice. And, you know, it's not like it's just a challenge to chop. I mean, that's that's my job as a coach, right? I mean, when a guy's playing well, I got we got to get him to play better. And when a guy's not playing well, we got him to play better. I mean, so Chap and I have an awesome relationship and I love the guy and he's worked his butt off and, you know, I'm going to keep telling him regardless how good he thinks it is. I think he can be better than even he thinks he can. And I think that's important for a coach to do with a player that he truly cares and believes about and I love the guy. >> I know you mentioned Austin Jackson and the line played well last week. We do like to ask head coaches questions that fans ask us a lot. >> You like to ask me a lot of questions. >> I do. Yeah. >> Could you see any scenario barring injury where Proctor plays tackle at all this year or you and Sully committed to leaving him the full year at guard under any circumstances excluding injury? >> I mean you're asking me like a huge hypothetical with anything that could happen. So sure there could be something that happens after the way you phrased it. Not the way I'm phrasing it. So, sure, but you that's not like a blanket statement for me. That's an answer to in any scenario could Yeah, of course, anything could happen. >> I guess one follow with that would just be have you and Sully had any conversation that you're able to share where you had an opinion about whether you want to leave him at guard for the full year or whether you want to leave it opened? >> Um, Sully and I discuss a lot of things. Cincinnati obviously has um a lot of explosive plays offensively. What do you see as the biggest challenge in containing their offense? And also, how can your defense generate pressure without giving up big plays downfield considering who their QB1 is? >> That's what we've been working on all week. Um >> that you can share. >> Yeah, I mean, let me put it to you this way, right? When you when you look at this team, it starts the quarterback. I think he's one of the best quarterbacks in our league and he's had a ton of success. A ton of success and he plays the game the right way. Um, and he's super talented. And then you combine that with an offensive line that can protect. Take it a step further. And now I've already talked about Chase, right? And then you got Higgins and then you have a tight end who plays like a wide receiver. So, I mean, there there's a lot of things that you can't just pick one the whole entire game, right? So, you got to pick and choose as you go. What's the down and distance? What what scenario are we in the red zone? Are we on third down? And is it third and medium versus third and long? There's so many things that go into my head even as I'm just thinking about this right now, like who's the go-to in this situation that I think we got to stop, right? You can't stop everybody because if you try to stop everybody, you're not going to stop anything. So, you got to pick and choose. Um, and I don't want to leave out the back. You know, I think Brown plays the game the right way. Um, and he's probably not talked about a whole lot, but when I watch film, like he's the type of guy that you want to have on your team. He plays so damn hard. He runs violent, and I have a lot of respect for any back in this league that protects the way he does. He's a physical guy. And then the tight end, I mean, we talk about Gaseki all the time as a wide out, but you look at Sample and you look at the career that he's had and the physicality that he's had and all the stuff that he does in protection that he does for his team. I mean, that's a good offense over there. So for us, we're going to embrace the challenge of all those pieces. You know, whoever they finally figure out who we're playing against and based on down, distance, field position, where we are in the game, what we need to do, what we need to stop, we're going to have to throw a lot of different things at them, and that's going to be a huge challenge. But that's what makes this exciting because anytime you get to go up against a team like this from a coach's standpoint and a player standpoint, I mean, that's that's why we coach and play. >> Quick follow up on Brown. How does his ability to make catches out the back field kind of put uh pressure on your defense? I think he had like 11 last game. >> Yeah. Um you know, we've been playing a lot of really good backs. I mean, if you look back from week one to um obviously the Chiefs with Walker, um every week we seem to play a guy. Aaron Jones last week. Um you just got to keep an eye on them and it just, you know, when they catch the ball, we got to get 11 hats to the ball. Everything we do defensively is going to be guys all year long is can we keep playing is with great communication, which we played better the last two weeks, with great physicality and can we get 11 to the ball? Like that's my challenge. Can we get 11 to the ball consistently so when I go to tackle you, I can take my shot cuz I know I got 10 of my guys ready to come and help me out. That has to be how we play this year. And if we do that in those positions and you catch the ball, then then we should we should be in pretty good shape. >> How has Chris Bale done so far? And can you put a percent on where he is? We understand that Atlanta was his first contact in months. Where where is he as far as his progression? >> Yeah, I don't know if I could put a percent on it. Um, but while that's a good question, I just I think me just throwing out a number would be just me throwing out a number, you know, is he is he is he ahead? Is he behind? He's probably ahead for where I thought he'd be just because the guy missed training camp, you know what I mean? And and I think Chris is a guy when you talk to him and and I think you guys probably had Chris is one he's an awesome guy and he's one of those guys you love. He's so damn competitive. He blocks the run after the catch. He runs angry and you can start to feel him gaining confidence and he needs to do that and he needs to play and he needs the experience. He just he missed so much time where he's just still in that catchup mode. Um but I had a great talk with him yesterday, man. like that guy's he's doing everything right and and I totally believe in him and I have all the confidence in the world in him and um putting at a percent all I know is this he's going to get better and better and that is exciting. >> Michael Taff was telling us that he didn't want to disclose what it was obviously but he said they've done something to solve the communication issues. I know it's a week- toeek thing and you're only as good as how you play Sunday. Uh he also said that players are meeting on their own some. Have you liked what he and the other young defenders have done to try to fix those issues? >> Yeah, and and I think a lot of that too is just going to come with time playing together. I think it's a lot of things happen fast. Okay. So, there's a lot of subtle things that you have to get to where it's you almost got to be able to finish each other's sentences and kind of, hey, look at them a certain way and I know what that means and it just it takes time. So, by those guys getting together and meeting on their own, it's going to help because they can communicate when they watch film. Um, I think a ton of them went out to dinner last night and I just think being around each other and connecting and growing together. I think it's all really, really helpful. >> Coach, the game on Sunday is a crucial catch game. The Dolphins will celebrate that they raised $100 million for cancer for the South Florida community. I wanted to ask you uh how do you feel to be in a team like that that is so connected to the community and does this kind of activities? >> I I think it's awesome. Um everything that they do for the community. Um I think it's outstanding and and I am just honored to be a part of that. Um you know with the catch for cancer that's close to me. I lost my father to cancer. My mother had cancer. Um, so when I wear that sweatshirt and there's anything that I can do to help, I do not take that lightly. And I'm glad that one the NFL supports it and I'm glad that our team takes it to another level with all the support that they give. Uh, from Mr. Ross all the way down and that that's a big deal to me and and and just very very proud that I can help any way that I can. >> Last question. Have we've talked a lot about um Jacob Rodriguez, his relationship with Jordan Brooks, your relationship with Jacob. Um how would you describe it considering you know you're a defensive coach, you're in his ear with the green dot and everything like that? What is it kind of like a coach quarterback relationship just on the other side of the ball? >> Yeah, I I think that's a great way to put it. Um you know, I'm probably in contact with him as as much as I am with any other player for that reason. And then on game day, take it a step further. It's it's really me and him talking through the whole entire game. Um, so it's it's exactly like you just said, it's like a offensive play car with a quarterback. It's a defensive play car with a mic linebacker. Um, I love Jacob. I trust him. I have total confidence in him. Um, I think there's I think he's got so much great football ahead of him. I just I love the way he works. I love him the way he approaches the game. I've said it over and over again. He's a super person off the field. I I have a great connection with him and um that's going to just continue to grow in time just like it will with all these guys that were going through this journey together. Um but yeah, that's that's a a very very good way to put it the way you did. >> All right, guys.

I mean, it's hard to plug a tight end into the backup fullback spot and expect the same efficiency because that the center of gravity is different with you. He's actually shorter, which I think makes him more effective at that tight end position. I think 11 personnel for the 49ers, three wide receivers is something that's going to have to be a thing. I think the Seattle trap is also a real thing. I think the Seahawks want you to run heavy personnel because they're so good at combating it cuz they're heavier than a normal nickel package. Remember the Rams ran all that nickel in week one against the 49ers and that meant the 49ers could just run it all over, steamroll the Rams. The Rams are not built like the Seahawks. The Seahawks can stop the run out of nickel. The Rams obviously can't stop the 49ers run out of nickel. So, different game calls for different strategy. You're obviously going to have to have a diversification of personnel if you're the 49ers, but I think Debo Samuel gives them a very, very interesting card to play because he's an adaptable player. You could be in three wide receiver 11 personnel, but he can always chipped into something that's closer to the line of scrimmage, maybe even the back field. And he more importantly, he could punish defensive backs. And it doesn't matter if it's Nikki Manuri or, you know, you could go through any list of defensive backs in the league. Debo Samuel is also a unique player. He's also playing at a really high level. And it's just human nature. When a guy built like a brick is running at full speed with reckless abandon like Debo Samuel does, another human being doesn't really want to step in front of him. So, in that regard, I think it's going to be a very, very key Debo Samuel game for the 49ers. I mean, it's it's all hands on deck. All available hands on deck because uh Seattle is damn good. The 49ers are damn good. And uh this is a very very interesting early season matchup in that regard. Made even more interesting by the fact that Sebastian Valdez, the defensive tackle, has helped turbocharge this 49ers defense. He played the final year of his college career at Washington. He's been active for the first time in his NFL career here in his second year for the past two games. He's been really good active against the run, but he also eats up some grass chasing after QBs. We saw it against Boone Knicks last week. I thought it was a linebacker running down Boicks on the roll out, but it was a defensive tackle. It was the Hulk, Sebastian Valdez. And Kevin Gibbons, veteran 49ers DTackle, who made his NFL debut at Seattle in that great Dre Green Law game to close the 2019 regular season. He's almost like a coach for the 49ers now. He'll play a little bit coming off the practice squad. He'll be flexed up, but he helps the young guys a lot. Given has helped mentor Valdez. And well, I caught up with Sebastian in the 49ers locker room. >> This is back where you played your your final season of college ball. It's it's obviously exciting to go back to my uh my college and all that and see some good some guys that uh might stop by and whatnot, but it's it's exciting to go back and get the chance to see them. >> Obviously, it's been an exciting couple weeks for you. He said that he kind of helped you earlier this season when when you're trying to find a way to be active. What is a veteran presence like Kevin meant for? >> Man, it's it's a it's I can't thank him enough. I think having somebody like that who's been in my position, who's gone through that experience and can only guide you in the right direction, man, it's such a good help. And to have those type of guys in the locker room, it just speaks for what type of team this is, you know? So, super thankful. >> Out of, you know, just watching tape and getting a feel for for the NFL game, what what's been the most surprising aspect of getting into game action for you now that you've got some playing time under your belt? >> The surprising aspect, I'm not really sure. And um when you have a great week of practice, when you have such good habits and it it just translates to Sunday. >> So I guess the the way this team practices, it sounds like that that is a good replication of what happens in the game. >> Yeah, for sure. And um I don't think I think this team does such a great job. >> Well, as you can see, good good stuff from Sebastian Valdez. He and Carver Willis both played at Washington in different years, so they didn't overlap there. But Carver, the 49ers rookie offensive lineman. Really excited to head back to Seattle as well. And Sebastian is going to play in this game and he's going to play an important role. You cannot forget that what the 49ers did this past week was their best Dline effort without Nick Bosa, I think, since 2019. I mean, whenever they've lost Bosa, it's been a big big issue. I mean, there might have been some games in 2020 that that they really rallied when Carrie Haidider Jr. had that great year, but it's hard to think about 2020. That was that was a miserable year for for many different reasons. I thought what they did against Denver with all the wins they had up front, they didn't give up that touchdown again in the first half was massive for the 49ers defensive line. title: Zack Baun & More on Facing Jacksonville Jaguars
text: I'm feeling good. Really good. Really good. We're back. Had a full week of practice despite a little bit of limitations earlier in the week, but I feel really good. >> Are you officially out in the pro? >> Officially out. That's why I'm talking to you guys. Yeah, >> that's true. >> How was your >> How did that happen? >> Got hit in the head in the Bears game and uh >> didn't know it right away. Played through the rest of the game and then took another shot at the end of the game and just kind of added up. Woke up the next day feeling foggy, groggy, and big time headache. Uh, how was it sitting out and watching Todd and Campbell? It seemed difficult, but were you proud of the way they tried? >> Yeah, I was really proud of both those guys really. They went out and fought to the end and gave their best and it sucks we couldn't get the win and and finish on our terms. >> As one of the leaders on this team, what have you noticed this week and how everybody has coped with and reacted to the different news situations that have that have happened earlier in the week? The NFL is tough. Like, I've been in this league for this my seventh year now and I've seen guys come and go. You build relationships with guys and you never want to see guys leave or retire or get traded or any of that stuff. But as a leader now, you you got to say your goodbyes. Um, keep in touch with them and um move move forward. We have a full season ahead of us and we got to get things on track. When you look at this defense as a whole, I'm sure it was a different perspective watching it probably from a coach's angle last week. What are you seeing from this defense right now allowing the Rams to come back in that game? >> Uh, I'm I'm happy we got a couple turnovers finally. Um, we've been close on a lot of them. Um, a for I know a force fumble's coming, the sacks are coming. We continue to get interceptions now. Um, but we just got to finish. It's it's it's happened multiple games this year where um we let teams get not even towards the end, but just like one or two drives, they go go a long way and score points. We can't let that happen. >> This Jaguars offense all of a sudden is one of the highest scoring offenses in the league. What do you see from the Jags right now? >> Yeah, a really good scheme. I see good coaching. They're they're really well coached. um that mesh with really well, really good players and a a quarterback that's that's finding his groove and his rhythm in within the scheme. Um that all adds to points. >> Give them everything that's happening on the offensive side of the ball. What's the mentality from defensive side? >> We're not really worried about what happens on the offensive side of the ball cuz we know that if it's up to us, um we we can win a game, we can put a game away. Uh if if the opposing offense doesn't score, they don't win. So that's kind of our mentality moving forward. >> Beyond um you know going to bed tonight on on the plane, what what are some of the things that you guys have been instructed to do tomorrow to make sure that your bodies are ready to go for a Sunday? I >> mean, it started earlier in the week. Um we've been coming in earlier for practice for the day. Um they're advising us to get uh go to bed an hour earlier. um telling us our wake up times, our our our sleep times, when we should sleep, how we should sleep, and kind of how to go about this whole thing. >> What time you going to bed >> tonight? I I got to check. We're about to have a team meeting. Yeah. >> The past couple nights said like an hour earlier. So, what does that mean for you? >> Uh 9 or 10. >> Okay. >> Which kid is probably tough. >> Yeah. Yeah. Kids is tough. [laughter] >> Thanks, Z. Well, Fred, I know you're working your way back in practice. Just just how are you feeling right now? Uh, I'm feeling better than I was yesterday, honestly. Uh, you know, trying to work back in, uh, getting up to speed with, you know, conditioning and just being able to be a asset to the team that they need me this week. Um, you know, yesterday I took like a little step back, but today I felt great, felt good. Came in, got some treatment. Um, you know, ready for whatever opportunity presents itself on Sunday. >> How close do you feel like you would be ready to be full go 100%. Are you still there this week or or is it maybe a next week type of thing? >> No, I'm ready to go. I'm full go right now. I think I I think I you know, like I said, progressed this last couple weeks and you know, Steve, Tom, you know, the training staff did a good job of trying to bring me back up the right way, not the fast way. And uh I think uh just practicing today full speed against, you know, uh the defense and everything, getting real looks at like real contact. Uh I felt great. You know, guys are saying I was looking good. So go back and see what it looked like in a couple couple minutes. >> And I don't know if we've ever seen a crazier week in a specific position group's room. Can you take us through just what this week has been like through your perspective? [laughter] >> This week has been very surprising. Very surprising. And um you know just you know the lane situation is just you know that's our brother. You know we know what this game means to him. we know what this team means to him and you know whatever he needs for his mental whatever he needed you know we was ready to support him and you know we still support him even now and it's like bro go get your wrist you did you did enough and uh you know I'm excited to see what the future holds for him hopefully he gets that gold jacket sooner than later and uh you know anything that you know what else happened with Cam is just it was shocking but I mean it's the nature of the business at the end of the day it's year eight. There's not too much I haven't seen. It's not too much I haven't experienced myself. And uh you know, just got to keep the ball rolling. You know, tomorrow the sun going to shine. So, you know, Cam was a very important member to us and you know, we all was sad. We all, you know, hugged it out and you know, talked to him and you know, it just it was just a whirlwind of emotions, but you know, tomorrow's still going to come and that's the nature of the NFL. It don't last for long and everything happens too fast that you can't really, you know, process stuff till after the fact. What's the best way to describe how it's been in the offensive line room this week? >> Uh it's been it's been it's been good. It's been really uh just adapting. Just everybody got to adapt. Everybody got to do something. You know, everybody got to do something more. It's uh we down a lot. Uh you know, the guys in this room are ready to step up. They got to step up. You know, Markeel Willie, you know, Drew, you know, he had his injury and you know, he's trying to come back and you know, he's fighting every day. So why not fight for my brothers and be available and be ready to go if my numbers call. You know, only thing that matters is Sunday. We can't focus on nothing else. So >> veteran guy, Fred, any added emphasis from you to try to, you know, help the younger guys? >> I mean, yeah. Just really just trying to give everybody, you know, my little piece of experience. You know, I've been around. I've been multi- different teams. I've been cut. I've been waved. I've been traded. I've been everything. Uh, and I just want them to understand like, hey, don't be too high, don't be too low. Just go out there and try to do your your brand of football every player. If you mess up, go 1,000 miles the next play. It's not over till, you know, the clock is zero. So, just trying to, you know, keep everybody levelheaded. You know, it's a lot. It's a lot. We a young group. Despite me, Jordy and uh and Landon, I think we're we're relatively young and you know, these guys got a lot to experience. And it's just a step. It's just a it's just a uh it's just a path that you know, you got to experience in your first year. Some of them, you know, Markeel, uh Willie, you know, it's just the nature of the business. You got to you got to deal with the hiccups and keep the ball rolling. Speaking of the other teams in other cities, short time, [clears throat] but what was your stint in Jacksonville like? >> What was your stint in Jacksonville? >> It was good. I love those guys. Those guys was cool. Uh, you know, the head coach, everybody. I was uh I was really fond of the locker room and really fond of just the building and stuff like that. But, you know, I want to win. I don't I don't like losing revenge games. I don't I don't prefer it. you know, we played Cincy when I started 24 and you know, I had a tall task and that's basically what you know, we got this week. So, you know, my numbers are called whether whatever position it may be, uh, I try to do my best to, you know, help this team win. >> And you mentioned having the experience of so many years in the league, having the experience of being traded before, I think very few people can relate to that situation. And when you're here in the facility, everyone starts finding out. What is that like when you find out Cam Jurgens is traded? >> I mean, we didn't I didn't I didn't I didn't believe it. I didn't like I couldn't I was like, "What?" And then come to find out he he knew, everybody knew and we just wanted to say by our brother, you know, send him off the right way, you know, and uh you know, at times, you know, is what what was important was just you know, hey, thank you for everything. You know, we appreciate you. We love you. Go handle your business wherever you at. you know, the ball don't stop. Games are still going to be played. Football is still going to be run, you know, and you know, he was dealing with his uh with his with his concussion and, you know, it's just a roller coaster. I was just trying to, you know, help him understand like it gets it gets like you you going to have to get adjusted. Obviously, there's a there's an adjustment period, but they need you to go ball up, brother. >> And there's definitely a microscope right now at the offensive line room. Is Nick Seri spending more time in the room or are they trusting that you guys are going to work through this? >> I have 100% confidence in us. 100%. No matter who's up, don't matter if it's Jake, don't matter if it's Willie, no matter if it's me, don't matter if it's John, everybody know what's at stake. And what's at stake is our pride is all. And you know, the the nature of the business is, oh, we're down and out. Oh, you you're thinned out. You have nobody. You have two starters from the 53 starting this game. Who cares? Y'all not going to care if we lose. Nobody's going to care if we lose. Like, let's win. Why not? You know? So, that's the that's the that's the tall task we got. And I have 100% confidence in us. 100% confidence in [clears throat] these guys and this team. And, you know, don't count us count us out yet just because of what it look like from the outside. Jaylen was on the field to the offense after the news of Tuesday and Wednesday. >> Yeah, definitely. You know, um I think just the main thing is playing for each other. Just executing at a high level. It's really >> what have you had to do with the current round? >> Just making sure that we get our sleep. That's the main thing. Know it's only a 7-hour flight. Ain't too crazy. Just making sure that we get our sleep. We well rested for you know time out there. >> Get the sweep on the point. >> You had to adjust or I know you guys have practiced earlier like anything for you. >> Do you think there such a conversation especially like the Australia game became such a talking point. title: Germie Bernard PASSES Aaron Rodgers' test, Rico Dowdle's role, Injury Updates | Steelers Rewind
text: What's up, everyone?  Welcome back to Steelers Depot at pennlive.com. The Pittsburgh Steelers practice here on Friday ahead of their Sunday game against the Indianapolis Colts. Let's talk about it a little bit.  As for injuries, the situation hasn't changed much .  Anthony McFarland continues to work on his recovery.  Rico Dowdle continues to make progress in his return after his toe injury. Speaking with running back coach Ramon Foster, it seems like a very real possibility that we'll see Rico Dowdle this week.  As for other matters, Jaylen Warren participated lightly in the stretching exercises.  It's the first time he's done it all week.  That's a good sign.  He could be a limited participant or perhaps he is still not training. Certainly, it's not going to be anything alarming .  I don't think he's going to play.  So I think it's a good first step towards playing next week, which is when I expect to be back.  Jaylen Ramsey is still working on his wrist injury, but he'll almost certainly suit up and play.  So, in terms of health, the Steelers are doing pretty well, relatively speaking.  And if they get Dowdle back, even better.  I spoke with Ramon Foster about how he is.  How is Rico?  He said, "Rico will be a player who could surprise people." He thinks, you know, we've only seen one full game from Rico Dowdle, and that was in week one.  And in week two, he injured his finger very early on.  He dislocated it twice during the game.  He basically said that "Jaylen is obviously a phenomenal player, but they need to take some of his workload off." Although he could still be the lead runner.  That's the impression I got, that Jaylen will be the main runner, but that Rico can be the change of pace, the one who gives him a breather.  And they really like Rico's intelligence in reading the field , understanding the concepts and the small details.  So I don't expect Rico Dowdle to suddenly surpass Jaylen Warren in plays.  I believe Jaylen Warren will be the lead running back and a focal point of this offense.  But I do believe that Rico Dowdle will help prevent Jaylen Warren from taking hits every week and suffering so much wear and tear that he gets injured.  If they lose it, it would be a huge loss.  And he's dealing with a couple of things, you know, with his shoulder still.    He still has to overcome that injury, but he's a warrior and he'll pull through. The other guy, you know, that I talked about a lot today was Jeremy Bernard.  And I spoke with Jeremy today, Aaron Rodgers is actively probing him on minute details of game situation, the personnel, what that personnel does, the route, how he wants to run against this coverage, all these different things.  Up to the 75 sets of hand signals that Aaron has, which are in a document that Jeremy had to make sure he knew about.  And apparently , Aaron loves Jeremy Bernard.    I was talking to Adam Henry, who was his coach, and Tom Arth, the quarterbacks coach, and they told me that Aaron has been testing him all week, and Jeremy passed with flying colors.  So much so that Jeremy has earned Aaron Rodgers' trust.  And Rodgers rarely trusts rookies, but he really trusts Jeremy Bernard.  And Jeremy Bernard said he treats Aaron like just another friend.  Not like I was Aaron Rodgers.  He's not, you know, he's not a mystical being.  He's a guy too.  He's a joker.  And then, they became quite close.  So I'm really excited to see what this connection between Aaron Rodgers and Jeremy Bernard can lead to. Alright, folks, be sure to like, comment, subscribe, and turn on notifications for more. Thanks for watching.

I mean, to me, instincts, and you've probably heard me use this analogy before, is like you can teach somebody how to swing a baseball bat. You can teach strike zone is, but you can't teach them whether it's a good pitch to hit from the time it leaves the pitcher's hand, it gets to home plate. That's an instinct. title: Remembering The Legendary Mike Ditka: One Of The Most Iconic Figures In NFL History
text: Mike Ditka has passed away. University of Pittsburgh, great top five draft pick as a tight end, the first tight end to ever go into the Hall of Fame. Obviously, Super Bowl champion head coach and uh one of the most synonymous figures that the NFL has had for 40, 50 years at this point. Tough, hard-nosed, badass football player. Obviously, Chicago roots with Northwestern. Covered Mike Dicka. Knew Mike Dicka very well in the next hour to have a conversation. But AJ, you're talking about one of the toughest, baddest, uh, most interesting and entertaining men in the history of the league. AJ. >> Yeah. When you say most interesting and most entertaining, like that's how I remember Mike Dick. I don't I don't remember him as a coach. I see all the clips and everything of him as a player and a coach. I remember Mike Dicka as an unbelievable personality on TV talking about football and in great movies like Kicking and Screaming. He's an unbelievable youth soccer coach Willil Ferrell's dad in that uh that great [laughter] cinema that we all got to see back in the day. But yeah, Mike Dicka, he is Chicago. He is the Bears. He's what I think of when I think of the Bears a lot of times. >> Yeah. And uh we'll miss him for sure. And uh job well done, Dicka. Job well done, sir. We understand he's tough, but we didn't really get to know him and see him in a lot of different portions of his life. Could you maybe explain to us what Mike Dicka meant to you, the city, and uh all of sports during his run? >> Absolutely. The very first thing I ever got paid to do in this business, the first assignment I ever had for which I got paid was to cover the Chicago Bears draft back in the days when the entire draft was held on a Saturday. I drove to the old house hall and covered the Bears draft in 1992. And after they made their picks, we would sit in the in the media room and all of a sudden in walked Mike Titka in the sweater and the cigar. And when I tell you he was larger than life, I don't even know how. That's an overused phrase. He literally embodied it. He was like something at the center. Everything just sort of orbited around him. And I've told people many times over the many years because I worked and lived in Chicago for seven years after college in the local media. And people don't necessarily understand or believe this, but the truth of the matter is Michael Jordan was a global icon and certainly beloved in Chicago, but Mike Ditka was the biggest star in Chicago sports. And that is, in my opinion, it was inarguable. He was the most beloved figure in the city, and it extended those SNL sketches that everyone remembers so vividly. uh because he was the greatest player or one of the greatest players in the franchise's history at the point at which he was playing. You could have argued he was the best player and then he winds up coaching them to what remains their only Super Bowl championship. He remains to this day the only Hall of Famer to have played for a team and coached that team to a Super Bowl championship. He was the first tight end to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. He was a genuinely great player. He holds records that stand to this day for receiving. He really revolutionized the position um at a time when tight end had previously really just been a blocking position. He once told me, he grew up in Alequipa, Pennsylvania, as I assume you know, Pat, he once told me that if he had not made it in football, he wanted to be a dentist. And I've often laughed thinking about what it would have been like to walk into a dentist's office and find Mike Ditka sitting there ready to put those enormous hands in your mouth and figure out what was wrong. I'd love to tell you my favorite Mike Ditka story and then we can go anywhere you want. But you might remember Mike Dicka appeared on Mike and Mike in the morning every Monday. I want to say for at least 15 years, maybe more than that. So we got to know him extraordinarily well. I covered him in Chicago as a reporter, but my relationship with him really began when we were both at ESPN and he was extraordinary with us. He was unpredictable and fun and funny and opinionated and all of the things that you associate with Mike Ditka. But you might remember, or maybe you don't, that um Mike Olick, Mike Ditka, and I did two Monday Night Football games back in the early days when ESPN first got Monday Night Football. On the opening Monday night, there would be a double header. So there would be the primary broadcast team, which I think at that time was Mike Taro and John Gruden. And then the late game would be in in two consecutive years, was me and Goolick and Mike Dicka. And Susie Calber was our sideline reporter. And this is a night that I will remember for as long as I live. The game ends. We're in San Francisco. The game ends and they rush us to the airport. me, Golick, Ditka, Susie Culber, we're going to get on redeye flights and fly back to the East Coast. And I'm I'm sure, well, you fly a little differently than most people, but um most people have had the experience of getting on a red eye, you're tired, you're blurry, it's West Coast, everyone's boarding with pillows and all of this stuff. And we are racing in like a bad out of hell to try and make this plane. And we're going through security. And I notice out of the corner of my eye that in security they're giving Susie a problem with something. So I go over to try and help her. And you get like that horrible we land in Chicago where we're connecting through Chicago. He's getting off and staying in Chicago where he lived. How are you?" And he just sat there and that was it. Motionless and fine. He was Mike Ditka in every single way. He was as Mike Ditka in private as he was in person. He could be prickly. And I think the entire city of Chicago feels this way today as well. He was as iconic and as connected to a city as probably any sports figure has ever been. >> Thank you for taking us on that journey right there, man. obviously uh somebody that's very close to you. Thank you for joining us to explain who he is and what he meant to you because I uh fellow Yinszer uh only know him for being because we didn't really see him play. You only we only see the highlights and like well he's the toughest, he's the meanest, he's the baddest and as a coach he maintained that kind of lore and then when he gets on TV he becomes one of the most entertaining and informative people in the history of television. We are big fans of his. you being like close to him and giving us that perspective. We're very grateful for Greeny and uh we know this probably hard to talk about in this world, but there's very rare situations where a player becomes the first ever Hall of Famer at his position. He coaches a championship and then he's a lightning rod on a microphone. Greeny, I I mean, when did you guys know that he was going to be who he was microphone wise? Is that immediately day one when he gets in or as he's coaching, you know, that's going to be the case? When did you guys know his media career was going to be what it was? M Mike Ditka's media career while he was the coach of the Bears was the stuff of legend. His Wednesday press conferences. So I covered those teams in the early 90s. I covered him in 9192. I I think he got fired after the 92 season. Dave Wstead started 93 or 94. I've lost track of the years now, but however many years he remained as the coach. His Wednesday press conferences, I would have bought a ticket to go and attend them. He was so entertaining. He was he would you want to talk about going back and forth with the media. This was long before there was social media, but there were columnists in town and it's was the very beginning the infancy of sports talk radio and he would go at it with people. He would go at it with fans. He didn't give a damn. I worked at the first all sports radio station in Chicago. I was screening calls the day he legendarily said to a caller. A caller called in and said something they didn't like and he said, "Well, I tell you what, my address is something something North Washington," which was the address of the old Halis Hall. He said, "You call me up and you tell me what time you want to meet there and I will whip your ass." [laughter] My dick said that on the radio to a stranger. And that is exactly who he was. He was he was um larger than life doesn't even begin to tell the story. And he was completely unafraid to say whatever he wanted to say. He didn't give a damn. he was Charles Barkley before Charles Barkley. Um it it it was it most of his opinions were the oldest of the old school or he would have said um the way things are supposed to be like he just sort of viewed things very differently. He was as old school as it got. Um I'm trying to think of of what other ways I could to describe to you. Here's here's one thing that I said. Hembo, we did a book um a couple of years ago and he was one of the chapters in it. And so Hembo sent me the notes that we had on him that day and he reminded me of something I said which I genuinely believe that if Jerry West is the logo of the NBA, if the NFL were to pick a logo, Mike Ditka would be an excellent choice. There were very few people who had longerl lasting impact on the league than Mike Ditka did as a player starting at Pit and then in the NFL from 1960. He went into the Hall of Fame as a player. Is in the Hall of Fame as a coach. He is the only Hall of Fame player to win a hundred games or more as a coach. During his tenure as coach of the Bears, his teams won more games than any other team in the NFL during that time.
